newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil TBC rate cut to 1.74 pct in December- paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil TBC rate cut to 1.74 pct in December- paper.

text.p: Brazil's Monetary Policy Committee (Copom) has cut the Basic Interest Rate of the Central Bank (TBC) to 1.74 percent for December from 1.78 percent in November, newspapers said.

With the new TBC, the Central Bank maintained its policy of gradually reducing interest rates, without showing concerns over an eventual impact of the low rate on demand and imports and the need for slowing the economy.
Industrial activity, consumption, credit and inflation were key indicators to determine the new TBC, Gazeta Mercantil financial newspaper said.
Gazeta noted, however, lower interest rates do not ensure that the Central Bank will not put the brakes on the economy early 1997.
The Copom also set the first Rate of Assistance of the Central Bank (TBAN) at 1.90 percent for December from 1.93 perent in November, newspapers said.

The TBC, which is set on a monthly basis and was first introduced in July, is used as a reference rate for Central Bank rediscount loans and PROER credit lines granted for banks in the process of mergers and acquisitions.
The TBAN is a rediscount line rate for Central Bank financial assistance to banks.
